sentence: This project studies how Ewing sarcoma cells behave in the presence of immune cell populations in the tumor microenvironment.
This project builds image sensors that read out calcium and voltage signals from many neurons in freely moving mice and zebrafish.
This project tries to find out which prostate cancers should be treated and which can be safely managed without treatment.
This project develops technologies for imaging large biological molecules at room temperature with near atomic resolution to understand their structure and dynamics.
This project tests whether aberrant signaling that controls cancer growth leads to chromatin remodeling through degradation of a tumor suppressor.
This project supports adaptive clinical trials by analyzing multi-omic biomarker data and keeping analyses consistent across projects.
This project maintains knockout and knockin mouse strains for studying Type 2 immune responses in the gut, skin, and lung.
This project studies how semaphorin 7A helps breast cancer evade anti-tumor immunity and looks for immunoevasion mechanisms in renal cell carcinoma.
This project uses deep learning to tell sitting posture from accelerometer data and to measure sedentary behavior patterns.
This project tries to separate passive and active changes in the left ventricle that cause poor relaxation in heart failure.
This project studies the epigenetic foundations that let natural killer cells acquire both trained immunity and antigen-specific memory.
This project tests whether optical micro-endoscopic devices made with 3D printing can be developed for early stage cancer detection.
This project builds AI models that combine multi-omics, medical imaging, and clinical narrative data, even when some data are missing.
This project uses proteomics and genomics technologies to find markers of drug resistance in multiple myeloma cell lines and patient-derived cells.
This project produces and distributes reagents that let researchers study immune mechanisms and immunization in nonhuman primates.
This project develops a digital therapeutics tool that aims to decrease self-stigma among pregnant and postpartum women with opioid use disorder.
This project tries to find genes that cause primary ciliary dyskinesia using a CRISPR screen and tools that distinguish key cellular features.
This project studies the molecular mechanisms by which tyrosine kinase inhibitors cause sinoatrial node dysfunction in non-small cell lung cancer treatment.
This project studies isoform-specific function of Bruno1 in RNA regulation during muscle development in Drosophila melanogaster.
This project develops an intervention that pairs emotion regulation skills training with a mobile health application for psychiatric inpatients who misuse alcohol.
